2609.34636.title: MechReasoner: A Simulator and Benchmark for Mechanistic Reasoning in Qualitative Physics
2609.34636.paper_summary: This work introduces MechReasoner, a mechanistic qualitative simulator grounded in confluence-based qualitative physics, together with a benchmark for mechanistic inference. Current large language models (LLMs) generate fluent mechanistic descriptions that do not reliably follow from underlying structural and causal constraints. The benchmark tests whether answers preserve simulator-licensed ambiguity, quantified claims, episode-graph transition evidence, repairs, and trace-support judgments. Its 1,120 items are generated deterministically from admissible interpretation sets, component states, scenario restrictions, confluence constraints, and derivation steps across 18 catalog mechanisms and six task families. Each mechanism undergoes converter checks of structure and topology and behavioral checks against quantitative simulations. GPT-5.5 accuracy decreases as family-specific mechanistic complexity increases, from 76.1% in the lowest-complexity bucket (B1) to 38.0% in the highest-complexity bucket (B4). The negative association remains after controls for rendered-prompt and expected-answer length. These results show that qualitative simulators can support auditable NLP benchmarks for mechanistic inference.
2609.34636.paper_summary_zh: 這項工作介紹了 MechReasoner，一個基於融合的定性物理學的機械定性模擬器，以及一個用於機械推理的基準。當前的大型語言模型（LLMs）生成流暢的機械描述，但這些描述並不可靠地遵循基礎結構和因果約束。該基準測試答案是否保留模擬器授權的模糊性、量化的主張、事件圖轉換證據、修復和追蹤支持判斷。其 1,120 項目是從可接受的解釋集、組件狀態、場景限制、融合約束和推導步驟中確定性生成的，涵蓋 18 種目錄機制和六個任務類別。每個機制都經過結構和拓撲的轉換器檢查，以及對定量模擬的行為檢查。隨著特定家族的機械複雜性增加，GPT-5.5 的準確性下降，從最低複雜性桶（B1）的 76.1% 降至最高複雜性桶（B4）的 38.0%。在控制了呈現提示和預期答案長度後，這種負相關仍然存在。這些結果表明，定性模擬器可以支持可審計的 NLP 基準，以進行機械推理。
